newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan torrential rains kill eight, two missing.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan torrential rains kill eight, two missing.

text.p: Torrential rains in northern Taiwan took eight lives, with two still missing, state television reported on Saturday.
"Police this morning found eight dead bodies after Friday's floods in (northern) Hsinchu county took away 10 people," the television reported.
Police were still searching for the two reportedly missing, it said.
Friday's floods took away two passenger cars and one commercial vehicle and the 10 people inside the cars, local media said.
Exact damage of the floods were not immediately known.
The island has suffered heavy torrential rains since early June.
A cabinet statistics agency on Saturday estimated the June rains caused total losses of T$1.62 billion (US$58.3 million).
The agency attributed the relatively high June CPI growth -- 1.85 percent year-on-year -- to torrential rains and floods that hit the island in June, especially early in the month, damaging crops.

The cabinet's Council of Agriculture said on Thursday that another round of heavy torrential rains in southern Taiwan since June 30 have taken four lives and caused T$1.5 billion (US$54 million) in farms and crops damages.
